NOVELTY STATEMENT
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a monitoring/indication scheme using aggregate fault codes after tripping.
CALCULATED: Proposed mechanism departs by using thermal-electrical correlation analysis of normal operating telemetry to detect pre-fault degradation signatures.
ASSUMPTION: The failure physics connection is that IGBT and capacitor degradation increases junction temperature and ripple current during normal operation, creating detectable patterns in the telemetry before catastrophic failure.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing physical relation: Junction temperature rise (ΔT_j) is proportional to power dissipation (P_d) and thermal resistance (R_thj-a): ΔT_j = P_d × R_thj-a. Degradation increases R_thj-a and P_d, creating detectable temperature ripple correlation with electrical parameters.
Magnitude verification: For a 500 kW inverter, a 10% increase in thermal resistance would cause approximately 5-8°C temperature rise at 80% load, detectable at 5-minute resolution with typical inverter temperature sensors (±1°C accuracy).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Data processing unit (DPU): Off-the-shelf industrial computer (same class as existing inverter control system)
2. Analysis software: Custom algorithm processing existing telemetry (DC voltage/current, AC power, heatsink temperature, fault log)
3. Communication interface: Existing inverter telemetry export protocol (no new hardware)
4. Alert system: Integration with existing SCADA system (same class as standard monitoring)
ASSUMPTION: The DPU has sufficient processing capability to run correlation analysis on 5-minute resolution data streams for multiple inverters simultaneously.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - uses existing telemetry connections and SCADA integration
- Operability: SAME - operates in background without affecting normal inverter function
- Maintenance: SAME - requires only software updates, same as standard monitoring systems
- Cost class: SAME - minimal additional hardware cost, primarily software development
Conclusion: SAME burden class as standard monitoring practice with different mechanism (correlation analysis vs. post-fault codes)

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:
1. Collect 6 months of historical telemetry from 100 inverters (including those that failed and those that didn't)
2. Apply correlation algorithm to detect thermal-electrical signature anomalies
3. Monitor false alarm rate and prediction lead time
Instruments: Existing SCADA system, historical data storage
Pass threshold: ≥14 days average lead time before trip, ≤1 false alarm per quarter per inverter
Fail criterion: <10 days average lead time or >1.2 false alarms per quarter per inverter
Duration: 6 months of validation data
Kill criterion: Failure to meet pass threshold in validation period
